notes: WebSearch could not be used for this part: the session's search allowance was already spent (the one search tried was refused), and no search engine was read in its place. Everything below was found by opening known addresses with the kit's honest User-Agent, a second or more apart and with each site's robots.txt read first: the campaign websites the candidates filed with the Secretary of State (read by the kit's own files step on a scratch copy of the database: 13 of the 30 filed one; 11 were read and are confirmed below, and the two that were not are review items), each county's, city's and school district's own site, the Legislative Reference Library, the state parties' and local party units' own sites, the University of Minnesota's election archive, and two local news sites' own search pages (Eden Prairie Local News, McLeod County Chronicle). A candidate with a campaign site they did not file could have been missed.

Nothing citable was found for James Jawaski, Andrew Messner, Scott Cutsforth, Joe Kampa, Myron "Bruce" Eastlund, Maia Gunderson, Jared Festler and Taylor Zinkle. None of them filed a website, and none is named on the pages of their city, county or school district that were read (Monticello's and Blaine's council and board pages, Fairmont's council and board pages, the Little Falls and Waseca school board pages, Stevens County's Sheriff page). The Glencoe-Silver Lake district's own page 'Meet the GSL School Board Candidates' says no response was received from Donna VonBerge.

Not read, because the site asked scripts to stay out or refused them (nothing was worked around): co.wilkin.mn.us, ci.sauk-rapids.mn.us and ci.minnetonka-beach.mn.us (robots.txt shuts out every script but the big search engines), which is why James Jawaski's county, Joe Kampa's city and Tracey Breazeale's council have no page of their own here; mncourts.gov's Judicial Officer Directory (403); mn.gov/governor (a Radware CAPTCHA page); armstrong4council.com, stevenscountytimes.com and dfl57.org (a CAPTCHA redirect); the Scott County Republicans' endorsed and recommended candidates page (403, asked twice) and sd13dfl.org (403); wrightcountyrepublicans.com (402); pctribune.com's search page (robots.txt); the Benton County Herald's Elections 2026 story (cut off for non-subscribers); sd50gop.org, cd8gop.com, cd4gop.com, sd66.org, stevenscountydfl.org and sd56dfl.org (certificate or handshake failures; certificate checking was never turned off); sd7dfl.org, sd19dfl.com and washingtoncountyrepublicans.org (no answer). The Fairmont Sentinel's search page shows nothing without scripts. Two addresses tried by guesswork exist but are not these candidates' (andrewmessner.com is another person's page; votemaia.com is empty) and were dropped.

A robots.txt question for John, not decided here. Five sites let the kit's own User-Agent in but shut out Anthropic's reading agents by name (Claude-Web or Claude-User, with ClaudeBot and anthropic-ai): markbornformn.com (the campaign site Mark Born filed) and four newspaper sites, hometownsource.com (ABC Newspapers, the Sun papers, Monticello Times, Morrison County Record), southernminn.com (Waseca County News), mesabitribune.com and wahpetondailynews.com. This sweep is run by Claude, so it took that as addressed to itself. Mark Born's home page and Meet Mark page were read before the rule was noticed; nothing read there is kept, which is why he has only a review item. The newspaper sites were not read: one hometownsource.com search page was fetched before the check, and that copy was deleted without being read. Other parts cite hometownsource.com under the kit's own name, which its robots.txt allows; if John decides that is what counts, these sites can be read for this part's candidates too (the Coon Rapids, Blaine, Monticello, Edina, Little Falls, Waseca and Hibbing races are the ones it would help). Sites that shut out only training crawlers (Squarespace's switch: sd8dfl.org, alliewolfformnhouse.org) were read, since nothing read here trains anything.

party_support (a key the loader does not read, in the shape parts 0, 6 and 10 use): three listings where a party unit publishes its backing of a candidate for a nonpartisan office in words other than endorsement. The Senate District 49 DFL names Dirk Tedmon under "Local Candidates we support". The Senate District 35 Republicans name Pat Carlson and Brian Armstrong in a table of nonpartisan local candidates to whom the unit gives "our support and recommendation"; the page is called "Endorsements" in the site's menu, but the word endorsed is not used on it, and the unit's own sentence about those candidates' politics is not repeated here. They are kept apart from endorsed_by so that no page calls them endorsements; whether and how they are shown is John's decision.

No Republican endorsement could be recorded for Allan Kehr II or Mark Born. mngop.com lists statewide and congressional nominees only; the St. Louis County Republicans' 2026 endorsement page pictures five House candidates and not Kehr; the 8th Congressional District Republicans list 'HD 8A - Alan Kehr II' under '2026 Candidates' without the word endorsed; no site was found for the Senate District 66 Republicans. saintpaulrepublicans.us calls Mark Born an endorsed candidate, but says of itself that it is 'not an official website of the Republican Party of Minnesota, nor affiliated with them', so it is not a party's own page and was not used.

The Minnesota Historical Election Archive (University of Minnesota Libraries) is the source for the earlier runs under a party label of Allan Kehr II, Allie Wolf and Tracey Breazeale. It is a university archive of official returns, not a news organization, and is labelled secondary for the second reader to judge. Its page for 'Allan Kehr' of Duluth carries the note 'Born Allan Harry Kehr II' and ends with the 2022 Republican primary in House District 8A, the seat he is on the ballot for now; that is what ties it to this candidate. The birth dates the archive shows were not taken (it names a birth records index as their source); Allie Wolf's birth year is from her own campaign site.

The two district judges: incumbency rests on county notices of offices to be voted for, which name each seat's incumbent: Stevens County's own notice (official) for Melissa Listug, and McLeod County's notice as published in the McLeod County Chronicle (secondary) for Patrick Goggins. Neither says when the judge took the bench, and no page about either judge on a government's own site could be read, so neither has an official_page.

For the second reader: (1) 'elected 2014', 'elected 2020' and 'elected 2022' are written in 'from' where a page gives an election year and not the year a term began; the loader reads those as no year. (2) Stan Karwoski: the county's page gives both 'since January 2016' and 'first elected in a special election in November 2016'; only the year is used. His council seat is given a start (appointed 2001) and no end, because the page says '14 years' and 'before being elected mayor in 2014' without an end date. (3) Keith Vogt: the district writes 'Treasurer' and '(2019-2027)'; 2019 is taken as the year he joined the board. (4) Matt Lehman: the city's 'First Took Office: Jan. 1, 2002' is his start on the council, and neither the city nor his site says when he became mayor. (5) Jen McEwen is a sitting member whose roster record has no birth date, so the Legislative Reference Library's is given; its record of her service (Senate 2021-2022 in District 7, 2023 to now in District 8) agrees with the roster. (6) Tracey Breazeale's council years: her site gives none; the archive's 2024 page says 2019-present, which is quoted in the source and not used as a start year. (7) Sam Rosemark's school board seat: the district gives the end of his term only. (8) Allie Wolf's own words are three words from a longer sentence on her Issues page about ranked choice voting: 'I want to make it easier for you to vote DFLers like me and Republicans like Greg Davids out of office.' (9) Karen Gabler's Experience page also lists a 'Community Education Services Advisory Committee: 2015-2021' without saying whose committee it is; it was left out. (10) Where a source is quoted in several short pieces ('Pat Carlson', 'At Large', 'Term expires: December 31, 2028'), the page shows them on separate lines of one entry. (11) Read and left out on purpose for everyone: jobs and employers, schools, military service, family and household, faith, health, and seats on private boards and associations.

For whoever holds Brian Kirkham (race 2026-MN-0392-003, Regan Birr's opponent): the Senate District 31 Republicans' 2026 Voting Guide names him under 'Recommended for the Anoka County Commission', 'District 2': https://www.sd31gop.com/voting-guide.html

Verifier, 2026-10-02: every address in this file was asked for again with the kit's own User-Agent, a second or more apart, and each recorded statement was looked for in the page's text (Moorhead's board page keeps its text in the page's data, where 'Keith Vogt', 'Treasurer' and '(2019-2027)' were found; Stevens County's notice is a PDF read with ballot/pdftext.py). Not opened: sd8dfl.org and alliewolfformnhouse.org, whose robots.txt names anthropic-ai and ClaudeBot (no Claude-Web or Claude-User line); the findings resting on them are listed under 'removed' with the reason, and are not shown to be wrong. dfl.org/endorsed carries no year, but lists this year's ticket (statewide offices and all 67 Senate districts), so it is taken as the 2026 list. The Senate District 35 Republicans' page still does not use the word endorsed, and the Senate District 49 DFL's page still lists Dirk Tedmon under 'Local Candidates we support', so the party_support entries stay apart from endorsed_by. The archive pages show full birth dates and other personal details; none is in this file. Jen McEwen's full birth date is from the Legislative Reference Library, an official page.
